terms.gloss: a tune, a melody (usually plural, modī)
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.106: flēbilibus modīs concinere (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 7.2: saltāre ad tībīcinis modōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The measured run of the notes: melody, rhythm and time together. Mostly plural: flēbilēs modī, a sad tune. The everyday sense of modus is a measure, a limit, or a way (see manner).

terms.gloss: a song or tune, sung or played
terms.comment: The singing or playing itself; see song.

evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.41: vōx absona atque absurda (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a voice or instrument off the note; also, more generally, out of keeping with something.

phrases.english: What’s that tune you’re singing? I don’t know it.

sources: Lewis & Short: modus · Lewis & Short: cantus · Lewis & Short: absonus
